title: autopilot step 2 of the ledger removal: gate advancement is re-decided from its observed fingerprint with no once() ledger entry, and a PR that has landed is never gated or reported
acceptance: Why. The autopilot's gate step still runs through the `once()` write-ahead ledger (`once` at bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:201-214, `recover` at :216-221). `advance()` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:142-220) wraps the gate launch in `self.once(['advance', fingerprint], task, gate)` at :220. Any error inside `gate()` parks the action as 'uncertain' forever and queues 'Mechanical action needs reconciliation: <error>'. On 2026-10-05 this woke firstmate with 'authoritative head changed; regate before accepting' after a routine branch update, when the next poll would simply have re-read the new head. The same night, after #179, #180 and #181 merged through their captain cards, a gate the autopilot had started on the merging head finished afterwards and queued '<task>: stopped at gate 6' for an already merged PR, three times. This task is step 2 of the approved ledger removal (T-190 did branch updates): the `advance` class leaves the ledger, and a gate, protocol or review result for a PR that has landed is dropped. The `recheck`, `restack`, `launch-review` and `pr-event` ledger classes stay as they are; later steps take them.

Why `advance` next. Of the four remaining classes it is the only one that fires on every poll for every open PR. Its fingerprint (`key([pr number, head, base sha, checks, bound verdict, authored details, merge-slot release])`, :208-209) is already a complete observable predicate, so the ledger adds only the 'uncertain' park and its wake. The merged-PR bug sits on the same path: the gate this step launches is the gate whose late result woke firstmate.

Per-PR advance record replaces the ledger. `advance()` no longer calls `once()`. Instead `data['advanced']` (a new state field defaulting to `{}`, added to the defaults list in `Pilot.__init__`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py about 61-63) maps the PR number (string) to `{head, fingerprint}`. If `data['advanced'][number]` already has the current fingerprint, `advance()` starts nothing. Otherwise it runs the gate step, and after `start_job` returns without raising it writes `{head, fingerprint}` and saves. The order is deliberate: act, then mark. A crash between the two costs at most one repeated gate (gates are read-only checks, and `busy(task)` holds a second launch while the first job is running), never a gate that is silently lost. A changed fingerprint on the same head (new CI, new bound verdict, new details, a merge-slot release) gates again exactly as today. Tests: two `advance()` calls with an unchanged fingerprint start one gate; a restart between them (the existing `test_restart_replays_no_gate`, tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py about 153-165) still starts one gate; `data['actions']` stays empty after any number of advances.

Pruning. `prune_branches` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py:13-22) also prunes `data['advanced'][number]` when the head changes or the PR is terminal: add 'advanced' to the `('holds', 'updates')` tuple at :19. `advance:` retry tokens are already pruned there by head. Test: after a head change, the old advance record and its retry token are gone, and the new head gates once.

A landed PR is never gated and never reported. Add one helper on the loop class, `landed(task, pr)`, true when either (a) the project's event rows (`self.rows()`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:24) hold a `merged` event for this PR number (compare as strings, since event `pr` fields are ints and state keys are strings). A merged PR cannot reopen. A `closed` row does not count, because event rows are never removed and `observe_pr` (:49-60) writes at most one row per PR and kind, so a reopened PR would keep its old `closed` row. A result for a PR closed without merging still reports as today. Or (b) a merge decision for this task (`kind == 'merge'`, `task == task`, `pr` equal to the PR number) in `state/pending/` or `state/decisions/` with `expected_head` equal to this PR head has `chosen == 'A'` and `fm_merge_outcome.merge_outcome(record)` in ('running', 'merged'). It reads only local files, so it makes no GitHub request and needs no new stub. (1) `advance()` returns before gating when `landed()` is true. (2) `job_completed()` (:280-316) returns silently, with no attention, no merge card and no review launch, for kinds 'gate', 'protocol' and 'review' when `landed(result['task'], result['pr'])` is true. A failed merge (outcome 'failed') or a B/C answer is not landed, so its results still report as today. Tests: with a `merged` event row for PR 12, `gate_result(6)` queues nothing, `gate_result(0)` raises no card, and a review result with code 3 queues nothing; with a decision record chosen A, `merge: running` and the PR head, the same three are silent and `advance()` starts no gate; with `merge: failed` the gate 6 wake still appears; with a merge record for an older head, the current head is not landed; with only a `closed` row (a reopened PR), `advance()` gates and `gate_result(6)` still wakes.

Migration. A one-time upgrade flagged `migrated_t193`, placed right after the `migrated_t190` block in `Pilot.__init__` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:67-75) and following its pattern, removes every `data['actions']` entry whose stored `identity[0] == 'advance'`, in any state ('started', 'done' or 'uncertain'), and removes from `data['wakes']` the undelivered `autopilot-`+key([project, 'action-'+token]) wake for each removed token. Files already delivered under state/wake-queue/ are untouched, and nothing is requeued. It runs before `serve()` calls `recover()`, so a 'started' advance is never turned into a fresh 'Autopilot stopped during an action' wake. Effect on work in flight: because the hashed fingerprint stored in an advance identity cannot be mapped back to a PR number, `data['advanced']` starts empty, so each open, non-draft PR with settled CI and no live round or busy job is gated once more on the first poll after the upgrade. That is one extra read-only gate run per such PR, and it can raise at most the card the existing merge-card dedupe (:337-341) already allows. A gate job running at upgrade is unaffected: `jobs` and `recover_jobs` are not touched by this task. Advance actions parked as 'uncertain' before this change are dropped with their undelivered wakes; the next poll re-decides them from GitHub state, which is what a reconciliation would have done. Tests: start with 'started', 'done' and 'uncertain' advance actions, a 'started' `restack` action and an undelivered plus a delivered advance wake. After two startups, each followed by `recover()` and `flush()`: only the restack action remains, and it is turned to 'uncertain' with its own wake, as today; the undelivered advance wake is gone; the delivered file is byte-identical; the second startup changes nothing; `migrated_t193` is true.

Existing tests that assert the old ledger behaviour change in place:
- tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py `test_update_migration_preserves_advance_and_delivered_files_across_two_startups` (about 455-480): keep its T-190 assertions, but the parked `advance` entry is now removed by `migrated_t193`, so `data['actions']` ends `{}`. Rename it so it no longer says 'preserves_advance'.
- tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py `test_nonancestor_keeps_stale_binding_park_and_wake` (about 474-484): a raising `authoritative_head` now gives an `advance:12:<head>` retry and, after the third due poll, one wake. No 'uncertain' action. The local ref stays at 'd'*40 and no gate starts.
- tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py `test_parked_advance_survives_migration_and_sync` (about 522-535): replace with a test that a parked advance is removed by the upgrade and that the next sync poll at an equal ref gates once.
Other callers of `advance()` or `job_completed()` that need no change, because none of them writes `merged` event rows or a matching merge decision: tests/lib/autopilot_jobs.py (about 31, 52), tests/lib/autopilot_task_resolution.py:89 and tests/lib/preflight_lifecycle.py (about 135). tests/lib/run_project_turns.py writes a chosen-A merge decision (about 136-140), but its stubbed fm-decide card has no `pr` or `expected_head` (about 69-71), so rule (b) cannot match. tests/lib/autopilot_turn.py:40 already skips merged and closed PRs. No other test file asserts on advance ledger entries: `grep -rn "'actions'" tests` shows only these and assertions that `actions` is empty, which keep passing. tests/lib/autopilot_turn.py and tests/lib/run_project_turns.py call `advance()` and `job_completed()` synchronously without merged events or merge decisions, so `landed()` is false there and they need no change; confirm by reading them.

Docs, edited in place in their home sections (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md):
- design/design.md §15.8 'Pilot and advanced integration', the paragraph beginning 'Branch updates are re-decided from GitHub state' (about 5188-5195). Say that gate advancement is also re-decided from its observed fingerprint without a write-ahead record; that a race on the authoritative head is re-read on the next poll; that gate-step failures retry at offsets 0, 1 and 3 and then wake once; that `migrated_t193` drops legacy advance actions and their undelivered wakes; and that the remaining write-ahead classes are re-check, restack, review launch and PR events. Replace the sentence 'Parked advance actions remain for firstmate reconciliation; their stored identities cannot establish why they failed.'
- design/design.md §15.8's '#### Autopilot owns PR advancement (T-175)' (about 5245-5268): add, in the paragraph on failed gates, that a gate, protocol or review result for a PR that has merged, or that has a captain merge chosen A at that head which is running or merged, is dropped without a wake, and that such a PR is not gated. A PR closed without merging is not covered, and its results still report.
- docs/autopilot.md, the paragraph 'Branch update steps no longer write reconciliation records…' (about 50-54): the same facts, with the same wording about merged PRs and chosen-A merges (and nothing about closed PRs). Replace 'delivered wake files and parked advance actions remain unchanged' with: delivered wake files remain unchanged, and legacy advance actions with their undelivered wakes are removed by `migrated_t193`.
- The module docstring of bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py (:1-6) says jobs have durable write-ahead identities. That stays true; it needs no edit.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from `tests/autopilot-loop.test.sh` (autopilot_loop.py) and `tests/autopilot.test.sh` (autopilot_cases.py): the new landed, migration, race and retry tests are red on base and green on head. Each test module stays under 1200 lines; if autopilot_loop.py would pass that, put the new landed tests in a new module, tests/lib/autopilot_landed.py, run by a new tests/autopilot-landed.test.sh in the same style as tests/autopilot-loop.test.sh. Every new test module that can reach a card sets `os.environ['HERDR_ENV'] = '0'` at top level, as tests/decide.test.sh:1024 requires. bin/ci.sh discovers tests/*.test.sh and balances shards by itself (bin/ci.sh:15-20), so a new suite needs no edit there.

Ordering and overlap. No other task in flight edits these files (T-190, T-191 and T-192 have merged). Firstmate dispatches T-194 to T-196 in parallel only if their scopes do not touch bin/lib/fm_autopilot*.py or design §15.8. `depends_on` stays empty because T-190 has merged.
